sections_target.text: This document sets out the washing of tension insulators on towers of 66 kV using a mobile washing unit. The document was prepared by Eng. Karam Gouda Mohamed of the Ismailia Lines Department, reviewed by Eng. Mohamed Nasr Mohamed, Manager of the Ismailia Lines Department, approved by Eng. Abdel Aziz Attia Abou El-Fotouh, General Manager of West Canal Lines, and revised by Eng. Mohamed Omran (for the General Manager of Development and Quality Control). It was field-tested by Eng. Mohamed Moslem Salem on the Shabab Generation / Shabab 2 line on 2 February 2005, approved by Eng. Farag Ali El-Azab, Head of the West Canal Networks Sector.

items: The work order must contain the names of the workers, the day, time and place of work and the tower number; the work order may be given by radio if the work is far away.
Every person and every item of equipment at the work location and the resistance of the water used shall be recorded in the work order.
Any drop in water pressure requires the water jet to be directed away from the insulator, conductor and tower.
It is essential to make sure communication is achieved between the work supervisor and the nearest station to the work location.
Make sure there are no broken discs in the insulators; washing shall not be carried out if the number of broken discs exceeds one third of the total number of discs in the insulator string.
Work must be stopped in the following cases: rain, lightning, thunder, storms, fog, high wind, at nightfall or when visibility decreases.
Workers shall avoid any equipment or wet ground during washing.
The resistivity value shall not be less than 1300 ohm/cm.
No solvents shall be added to the water used in the washing process.

Work must be stopped if the wind speed exceeds the following values: * For washing tension insulators with an angle up to 20 degrees (8 m/s) * For washing tension insulators with an angle from 20 to 45 degrees (6 m/s) * For washing tension insulators with an angle over 45 degrees (4 m/s)
All workers shall stand away from the earthed equipment at a distance of not less than 2 m.
Mobile washing unit — water tank trailer — mechanical washing unit.
Hose, 40 m long, with additional sections from 20 m to 100 m.
Nozzle, diameter (5-8 mm), fitted with an earth.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, water-repellent overalls, etc.
Wind speed measuring instrument, water resistance measuring instrument.

sections_target.text: Instructions the work supervisor must follow before going to the site:

rows: Determine the type of equipment to be used according to the nature of the terrain (agricultural tractor with trailer — small unit — transport truck).
Make sure the tank is filled with water.
Make sure the water hoses are sound (not cracked, not punctured, the assembly couplings tightly fastened, the hoses or the nozzle not blocked).

Make sure the pump engine is sound (carburettor, distributor, battery, fuel tank, radiator water), checking this with the competent workshop; the team then starts the engine and makes sure it is sound before going to the site.
Make sure the pump is sound (the pump packing is sound, to obtain the required pressure).
Make sure the nozzle earth and the equipment (truck) earth are sound (no cut in the earth cable, and the earth clamps tightly fastened to the cables).

sections_target.text: Instructions the work supervisor must follow upon arriving at the site:

rows: The person in charge of the work determines the wind speed and direction, and accordingly determines the suitable place for the washing equipment next to the tower, opposite the wind direction, and determines the sequence of work.

The technician assigned to operate the water machine runs the machine for not less than 5 minutes before preparing the machine to pump water (when the pump engine runs on petrol), and the water tank cover is opened.
The person in charge of the work measures the water resistance.
The linesman climbs the tower carrying (pulley + service rope + sling + weight).
He fixes the pulley at the top middle of the tower, at the level of the stay of the second travelling platform.
After fixing the pulley on the tower, he hangs the weight at the end of the service rope and lowers it from inside the tower formations.
The hose is fixed with a sling, leaving 2 metres of hose at the fixing point.
The washing man takes his place between the two circuits at the level of the first travelling platform, and the nozzle earth is tied to the tower body.
The linesman gives a start signal to operate the pump to pump water into the hose.
The linesman tests the water jet away from the conductor, insulator and tower, then starts washing phases T-1 & S-2 for both circuits in the first direction, according to the wind direction.
After finishing washing phases S-2 & T-1 for both circuits, the nozzle earth is removed from the tower and the linesman climbs to the level of the second travelling platform.
The nozzle earth is tied to the tower body, and washing of phase R for both circuits begins, according to the wind direction, as shown in the drawing.
After finishing washing phase R, the nozzle earth is removed and he descends to the level of the first travelling platform.
Move to the other side of the tower and start washing phases R-3 & S-2 & T-1, repeating steps 7, 6, 5.
The linesman gives a signal to stop the washing pump and starts removing the nozzle earth and lowering the hose with the service rope.
The linesman removes the pulley and the service rope and comes down with them, making sure no equipment is left inside the work area; the washing of a 66 kV tension tower is thus complete.

Introduction
This document sets out the washing of tension insulators on towers of 66 kV using a mobile washing unit. The document was prepared by Eng. Karam Gouda Mohamed of the Ismailia Lines Department, reviewed by Eng. Mohamed Nasr Mohamed, Manager of the Ismailia Lines Department, approved by Eng. Abdel Aziz Attia Abou El-Fotouh, General Manager of West Canal Lines, and revised by Eng. Mohamed Omran (for the General Manager of Development and Quality Control). It was field-tested by Eng. Mohamed Moslem Salem on the Shabab Generation / Shabab 2 line on 2 February 2005, approved by Eng. Farag Ali El-Azab, Head of the West Canal Networks Sector.
Safety Precautions
The work order must contain the names of the workers, the day, time and place of work and the tower number; the work order may be given by radio if the work is far away.
Every person and every item of equipment at the work location and the resistance of the water used shall be recorded in the work order.
Any drop in water pressure requires the water jet to be directed away from the insulator, conductor and tower.
It is essential to make sure communication is achieved between the work supervisor and the nearest station to the work location.
Make sure there are no broken discs in the insulators; washing shall not be carried out if the number of broken discs exceeds one third of the total number of discs in the insulator string.
Work must be stopped in the following cases: rain, lightning, thunder, storms, fog, high wind, at nightfall or when visibility decreases.
Workers shall avoid any equipment or wet ground during washing.
The resistivity value shall not be less than 1300 ohm/cm.
No solvents shall be added to the water used in the washing process.
Work must be stopped if the wind speed exceeds the following values: * For washing tension insulators with an angle up to 20 degrees (8 m/s) * For washing tension insulators with an angle from 20 to 45 degrees (6 m/s) * For washing tension insulators with an angle over 45 degrees (4 m/s)
All workers shall stand away from the earthed equipment at a distance of not less than 2 m.
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Mobile washing unit — water tank trailer — mechanical washing unit.
Hose, 40 m long, with additional sections from 20 m to 100 m.
Nozzle, diameter (5-8 mm), fitted with an earth.
Insulated rope, about 50-60 m.
Pulley + weight.
Earth cable for the truck.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as protective goggles, safety helmet, water-repellent overalls, etc.
Wind speed measuring instrument, water resistance measuring instrument.
Procedures to be Carried Out
Instructions the work supervisor must follow before going to the site:
Determine the type of equipment to be used according to the nature of the terrain (agricultural tractor with trailer — small unit — transport truck). | 1.
Make sure the tank is filled with water. | 2.
Make sure the water hoses are sound (not cracked, not punctured, the assembly couplings tightly fastened, the hoses or the nozzle not blocked). | 3.
Make sure the pump engine is sound (carburettor, distributor, battery, fuel tank, radiator water), checking this with the competent workshop; the team then starts the engine and makes sure it is sound before going to the site. | 4.
Make sure the pump is sound (the pump packing is sound, to obtain the required pressure). | 5.
Make sure the nozzle earth and the equipment (truck) earth are sound (no cut in the earth cable, and the earth clamps tightly fastened to the cables). | 6.
Instructions the work supervisor must follow upon arriving at the site:
The person in charge of the work determines the wind speed and direction, and accordingly determines the suitable place for the washing equipment next to the tower, opposite the wind direction, and determines the sequence of work. | 1.
The technician assigned to operate the water machine runs the machine for not less than 5 minutes before preparing the machine to pump water (when the pump engine runs on petrol), and the water tank cover is opened. | 2.
The person in charge of the work measures the water resistance. | 3.
The linesman climbs the tower carrying (pulley + service rope + sling + weight). | 4.
He fixes the pulley at the top middle of the tower, at the level of the stay of the second travelling platform. | 5.
After fixing the pulley on the tower, he hangs the weight at the end of the service rope and lowers it from inside the tower formations. | 6.
The hose is fixed with a sling, leaving 2 metres of hose at the fixing point. | 7.
The washing man takes his place between the two circuits at the level of the first travelling platform, and the nozzle earth is tied to the tower body. | 8.
The linesman gives a start signal to operate the pump to pump water into the hose. | 9.
The linesman tests the water jet away from the conductor, insulator and tower, then starts washing phases T-1 & S-2 for both circuits in the first direction, according to the wind direction. | 10.
After finishing washing phases S-2 & T-1 for both circuits, the nozzle earth is removed from the tower and the linesman climbs to the level of the second travelling platform. | 11.
The nozzle earth is tied to the tower body, and washing of phase R for both circuits begins, according to the wind direction, as shown in the drawing. | 12.
After finishing washing phase R, the nozzle earth is removed and he descends to the level of the first travelling platform. | 13.
Move to the other side of the tower and start washing phases R-3 & S-2 & T-1, repeating steps 7, 6, 5. | 14.
The linesman gives a signal to stop the washing pump and starts removing the nozzle earth and lowering the hose with the service rope. | 15.
The linesman removes the pulley and the service rope and comes down with them, making sure no equipment is left inside the work area; the washing of a 66 kV tension tower is thus complete. |
